headline: Trading and banking boom drives record profits
summary_short: Goldman Sachs reported record Q2 2026 net earnings of $6.63 billion (+78% y/y) on net revenues of $20.34 billion (+39% y/y), with diluted EPS of $20.98 versus $10.91 a year ago.
summary_long: Net revenues rose 39% y/y and 18% q/q to $20.34B, led by a 53% y/y surge in Global Banking & Markets — investment banking fees +55%, FICC +32%, and Equities +72%. Net earnings rose 78% y/y to $6.63B; diluted EPS reached $20.98 (from $10.91) on higher revenue and a 4% y/y lower diluted share count from buybacks. Annualized ROE was 23.5%. Total shareholders' equity dipped 1.1% y/y to $122.74B despite the earnings gain, consistent with $4.00B of buybacks and $1.36B of dividends this quarter. The board raised the quarterly dividend 11% to $5.00/share, effective Q3 2026.

drivers.explanation: Record trading, underwriting and advisory activity across Global Banking & Markets drove the quarter, with the y/y comparison also flattered by 2Q25 provisions tied to the since-divested credit-card book.

Global Banking & Markets net revenues rose 53% y/y: investment banking fees +55% on equity/debt underwriting and M&A advisory, FICC +32% on rates and commodities, Equities +72% on intermediation and financing.
EPS growth (+92% y/y) outpaced net earnings growth (+78% y/y) because average diluted shares fell 4% y/y on continued buybacks.
2Q26 provisions were mainly wholesale-loan impairments; 2Q25 provisions included the credit-card portfolio, transferred to held-for-sale in Q4 2025 and no longer on the balance sheet.
Not explicitly attributed by the release; the q/q-to-y/y dip is consistent with $4.00B of buybacks and $1.36B of dividends this quarter outweighing net earnings to common of $6.40B.
Board raised the quarterly dividend from $4.50 to $5.00 per share (+11%), citing the strength of the firm's earnings and capital position; effective the third quarter of 2026.
